text: The ultrasound findings of bile duct dilation and a subhepatic mass in the setting of painless jaundice are highly suggestive of a malignancy obstructing the biliary tree. Given your significant smoking history, pancreatic adenocarcinoma is a primary concern, so I will request further imaging to characterize the mass. REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT scan is puzzling given the ultrasound findings, so I need to rule out choledocholithiasis or a small ampullary tumor that might have been missed. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: This discrepancy between the ultrasound showing a mass and the normal CT and MRCP is unusual, suggesting the mass may be within the gallbladder itself rather than the bile ducts. I need to evaluate for gallbladder carcinoma, which can present with Courvoisier's sign and obstructive jaundice if it involves the cystic duct or ampulla. REQUEST TEST: ERCP

text: The ERCP findings of a cystic duct filling defect with a patent common bile duct strongly suggest Mirizzi syndrome, where a gallstone in the cystic duct compresses the common hepatic duct.
